title: How long does a private chef home visit take in Dubai?
body_markdown:
A private chef home visit in Dubai takes the time agreed for your menu, preparation, cooking and handover; dinner service and clearing up need to be included explicitly. The useful question is not just how long the chef stays, but when your food will be ready. Agree arrival, meal-ready time and departure separately before confirming the visit.

Check [private chef visits in Dubai](/private-chef-dubai) and the [current visit plans and included hours](/private-chef-dubai/pricing) before agreeing a timetable for your menu.


**TL;DR**

- How long does a private chef visit take? Agree the full session around preparation, cooking and handover.
- myCHEF provides vetted chefs for home cooking and weekly meal preparation in Dubai.
- Household cooking, meal preparation and a private dinner need different schedules.
- Confirm arrival, food-ready time, service duties and departure before booking.


## How long does a private chef home visit take in Dubai?

**A private chef visit should have an agreed start, a clear food-ready time and a defined finish.** A description such as an evening visit does not tell you whether the chef arrives before guests, serves the meal or finishes after the kitchen is cleared.

[myCHEF](/) provides private chef services for home-cooked meals and weekly meal preparation, alongside private dining and catering. When enquiring, explain which service you need rather than asking for a chef for an unspecified number of hours.

Use this sequence to make the timing clear:

1. **Set the outcome.** Decide whether you want a meal ready to eat, prepared meals for later or a hosted dinner.
2. **Set the food-ready time.** Give the chef a serving deadline, not only an arrival time.
3. **Confirm the preparation plan.** Establish what happens before arrival and what happens in your kitchen.
4. **Define service and handover.** Clarify plating, serving, storage instructions and clearing responsibilities.
5. **Agree departure.** Confirm what marks the end of the visit and how changes will be handled.

This makes the schedule useful to both you and the chef. You know when the kitchen is needed, and the chef has a brief built around the work rather than an arbitrary time slot.

## Does household cooking take the same time as a dinner party?

No. Household cooking is organised around feeding your household; a dinner party is organised around serving guests. Weekly meal preparation adds another consideration: food needs to be portioned and handed over for later use.

Choose the format before discussing duration. A single dinner or celebration belongs to private dining or catering, even when the guest list is small.

| Visit format | Best for | What the schedule needs to cover | Main advantage | Planning constraint |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Household cooking | A meal for your household | Kitchen setup, preparation, cooking and the agreed finish | Centres the visit on your household's meal | You need a clear meal-ready deadline |
| Weekly meal preparation | Preparing meals to use later | Cooking, portioning, storage arrangements and handover | Separates cooking from the time you eat | Containers, storage space and instructions need attention |
| Private dinner | Hosting a single meal or celebration | Preparation, course timing, agreed service and clearing | Lets you plan around the guest experience | Guest arrival and course pacing affect the finish |

**myCHEF suits households seeking vetted private chefs for home cooking and weekly meal preparation.** The service still needs a specific brief: chef vetting does not replace agreement on the menu, kitchen access or duties included in your visit.

If you are organising a single occasion rather than recurring household cooking, the guide to [hiring a private chef for one dinner in Dubai](/blog/can-i-hire-a-private-chef-for-just-one-dinner-in-dubai) addresses that separate service choice.

## Why does private chef visit length vary?

The work involved determines the schedule. Guest count matters, but it does not describe the whole job: a menu with separate dietary versions or several serving stages needs a different plan from a shared household meal.

Discuss these factors before agreeing the visit:

- **Menu preparation.** Identify dishes that need preparation in advance and those that must be finished immediately before eating.
- **Number of portions.** State how many people will eat and whether you also want meals prepared for later.
- **Service format.** Explain whether food should be ready for you to serve or whether you need an agreed dining service.
- **Kitchen facilities.** Describe the appliances, usable work surfaces and storage space available to the chef.
- **Dietary requirements.** Flag allergies, ingredient exclusions and separate meal requirements before the menu is finalised.
- **Finishing duties.** Agree who handles portioning, food handover, washing up and the final kitchen check.

**Compare visits by the work included, not by duration alone.** A shorter proposed session is not a like-for-like alternative if it excludes tasks that another proposal covers.

Avoid adding a new dish after the schedule is confirmed without asking about its effect. Treat changes to portions, service or preparation as changes to the brief, even when they sound small.

## What time should the chef arrive before the meal?

The chef's arrival should follow the preparation plan and your food-ready deadline. Do not use the time you want to eat as the arrival time unless the provider has explicitly confirmed that arrangement.

For a household meal, give the time the food needs to be ready. For a private dinner, distinguish guest arrival from the first serving: welcome drinks and conversation are not the same milestone as dinner.

A clear written schedule separates these stages:

- **Kitchen access:** when the chef can enter and begin setting up.
- **Food ready:** when the household meal or first serving needs to be ready.
- **Service finish:** when any agreed dining service ends.
- **Kitchen handover:** when the agreed finishing duties are complete.


![Four scheduling stages from kitchen access through food readiness and service to kitchen handover](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/179905e6-7929-4e0a-ae5c-495d32946dbf/body-55e00500960e7001b9f587523ae5cde3.jpg)

*Food-ready time and kitchen handover are separate points in the visit.*


Keep the household calendar in mind. If someone else needs the kitchen during preparation, raise that before booking. The chef needs to know whether the space is available throughout the agreed session, not just when they arrive.

## What should I prepare before the chef arrives?

Prepare access and the kitchen information first. Do not start chopping ingredients or buying specialist equipment unless the chef has asked you to do so; preparation responsibilities should be part of the agreed plan.

A useful pre-visit checklist covers:

- **Access instructions:** the address, building or community entry process, parking arrangements and the person receiving the chef.
- **Kitchen equipment:** available appliances and any known faults or restrictions.
- **Working space:** clear surfaces and a place for ingredients and equipment.
- **Food storage:** space for ingredients and any prepared meals you have requested.
- **Serving arrangements:** plates, cutlery and serving dishes, with responsibility for supplying them confirmed.
- **Household priorities:** meal times, ingredient exclusions and any parts of the kitchen that should not be used.

For a Dubai apartment or villa, explain any access arrangements that apply to your property. Check requirements with your building or community rather than assuming the chef can enter immediately on arrival.

Send kitchen photographs if the provider requests them. A view of the cooking area and appliances is more useful for planning than a description such as fully equipped.

## Does weekly meal preparation include packing and instructions?

Weekly meal preparation needs an agreed handover, not just an agreed cooking finish. Confirm who supplies containers, how meals should be divided and what storage or reheating guidance will accompany them.

Describe the meals in terms of how your household will use them. Individual lunches, shared dinners and separate dietary portions create different packing requirements, even when the underlying dishes are similar.

Ask these questions before confirming:

- Will meals be packed into individual portions or shared containers?
- Who provides the containers, and are they suitable for the intended use?
- How will different dishes or dietary portions be identified?
- What storage and reheating instructions will be provided?
- Who receives the handover if you are not at home?

Do not assume a single storage period applies to every dish. Ask for instructions suited to the menu and follow the guidance provided for each meal.

For recurring visits, agree the same handover process each time. Consistent instructions make it easier for everyone in the household to use the prepared food correctly.

## Does the visit end when cooking is finished?

Not necessarily. Cooking completion, serving completion and kitchen handover are different milestones. Your booking should specify which one defines the end of the chef's work.

Ask about clearing in concrete terms. Washing cooking utensils, loading a dishwasher, clearing guest plates and removing event equipment are separate tasks; do not treat a general reference to cleaning as confirmation of all of them.

The same applies to serving. Food placed in serving dishes is not the same arrangement as a chef remaining through successive courses, and cooking support does not automatically establish who serves guests.

**Ask for the finish to be described as a completed task, not just a departure time.** For example, your brief can request that prepared meals are handed over with instructions before the session ends. The provider can then confirm whether that duty is included.

## How do I compare two proposed visit schedules?

Compare the outcome and responsibilities before comparing session length. Both proposals should refer to the same menu, portions, kitchen conditions and service expectations.

Check each proposal against the following points:

| Detail to compare | What you need confirmed |
|---|---|
| Arrival | When kitchen access is required |
| Food-ready deadline | When the meal or prepared dishes will be ready |
| Preparation | Which tasks happen before arrival and on site |
| Ingredients | Who sources and supplies them |
| Service | Whether the chef cooks only or also performs agreed dining duties |
| Handover | Packing, instructions and finishing responsibilities |
| Changes | How altered menus, guest counts or timing are handled |

A schedule that fits your preferred evening but leaves serving responsibilities unclear is not ready to confirm. Resolve the gap first.

Ask about price drivers without assuming that time is the only one. Menu scope, portions, staffing and additional duties all belong in the quotation discussion; the written proposal should show what you are agreeing to.

## FAQ


**How long does a private chef visit take in Dubai?**

A private chef visit takes the agreed time needed for preparation, cooking and the specified handover or service. Confirm arrival, food-ready time and departure separately so the schedule covers the work you need.

**Should I book the chef to arrive when I want to eat?**

Book the chef's arrival around the preparation plan, not automatically at your preferred eating time. Give the provider your food-ready deadline and ask them to confirm the required kitchen access.

**Does a private chef stay while we eat?**

The chef stays during the meal only when that service is part of the agreed booking. Household cooking, meal preparation and a hosted private dinner need different service arrangements.

**Is weekly meal preparation the same as a private dinner?**

Weekly meal preparation is organised around meals for later use, while a private dinner is organised around a single dining occasion. Portioning and storage handover matter for meal preparation; serving sequence matters for a dinner.

**Does cleaning count as part of the chef's visit?**

Cleaning counts within the visit when the relevant duties are included in your agreement. Confirm cooking utensils, surfaces, dining dishes and any other clearing tasks separately.

**Can I leave home while the private chef cooks?**

Agree unattended access with the provider before leaving home. Confirm entry arrangements, a contact person and how the meal or prepared food will be handed over.

**What should I send myCHEF to plan a home visit?**

Send myCHEF your date, Dubai location, household or guest count and required service. Include the food-ready deadline, menu preferences, dietary requirements and relevant kitchen or access details.

The most useful detail in your brief is what needs to be finished when the chef leaves. That defines the visit more clearly than an arrival time on its own.

For a tailored myCHEF enquiry, send your date, Dubai location, household or guest count and whether you need home cooking, weekly meal preparation or a private dinner. Add your preferred food-ready time and any kitchen access constraints so the proposed schedule answers your actual needs.
